title: GMP: A Benchmark for Content Moderation under Co-occurring Violations and Dynamic Rules
measurement_description: LLMs' ability to detect co-occurring content violations and adapt to dynamic moderation rules, including hate speech and discrimination based on religion, as part of a multi-label classification problem.
findings: Models tend to flag frequent violations but overlook long-tail co-occurring harms (which would include less common religious violations). Models fail to update judgments in response to rule changes, especially when moderation instructions diverge from general safety norms, suggesting they rely on perceived toxicity rather than rule-conditioned reasoning. This means models might over-block religious content if the rule permits it but it sounds offensive.
